hypothesis: The rule-derived bookkeeping and ranking are no longer the bottleneck. Offline, an ideal always-top-suggestion player matches the live query counts, and neither a 2-step lookahead nor a construction-weighted prior improves the mean or max. Joint-MAP final assembly never beats the parent's per-circuit pick, because at budget 18 almost nothing is left ambiguous. What remains is the 7B's deviations: off-list picks and malformed tags. The claim is that these are sampling noise at temperature 0.7, not a stable preference. Decoding the first ask of each turn greedily (T=0) should then remove most re-asks and format failures without any new veto. FALSIFIED IN PART on this batch: re-asks fell from 7 to 2 and format failures from 1 to 0, but greedy decoding reveals a stable preference. On turn 3 of 3 of the 4 one-NOT episodes the model deterministically picks C(0,0,0) on an untouched circuit, at 0.78 of the best entropy, which passes the parent's 0.75 floor.
behavior_changes: First ask of every query turn and first ask of the final-table prompt use temperature 0.0 (greedy decoding) instead of 0.7.
Re-asks within a turn (after a veto, parse failure, or missing per-circuit lines) keep temperature 0.7, so a repeated ask can still produce a different reply.
preserved_behaviors: Everything else is byte-identical to the parent: rule-derived joint (split, A, B, C) space, compact per-turn state, top-4 joint-entropy suggestions, veto of answered/implied queries, the 0.75 information-floor veto with the floor dropped on the 4th ask, early stop once all circuits are determined.
Final stage: per-circuit line parsing, snapping each circuit to the nearest consistent table, most-likely fallback.
Frozen solver (self.llm only, temperature is a call argument) and label-free (env.query only); no branching on inventory or instance index.
verification: Offline (scratchpad sim reusing the parent's enumeration, ~100-150 sampled truths per inventory): greedy joint entropy vs a 2-step expected-information lookahead gave 3/3/1 mean 12.42 vs 12.43 (max 16 both), 1/5/2 12.26 vs 12.35, 3/3/2 14.87 vs 14.77 (max 17 both). Belief prior uniform vs construction-weighted: mean -0.3 to -0.5 but the max is the same or worse. So I did not change the ranking.

Offline endgame check at budget 18 with always-top greedy: unresolved episodes were 0-3/150 on 3/3/2, 2/4/3, 1/5/3, 3/3/3 and 2/4/4. Joint-MAP final pick vs the parent's per-circuit pick: identical correctness, 0 jointly inconsistent guesses. So the final assembly is not a failure point either.

risks: Net effect on query efficiency is neutral to slightly negative on this batch (mean 10.4 vs 10.2, within noise). The 0.78 turn-3 pick is a systematic cost on 1-NOT inventories that sampling at 0.7 had sometimes avoided.

Greedy decoding makes the model's biases deterministic. Any stable bad habit (here: (0,0,0) on a fresh circuit) now repeats on every episode with the same state, not just some. It can still only pass if it is above the inherited 0.75 floor.
Correctness cannot separate this from the parent here: both are 10/10 and nothing ends ambiguous. The case for the change is fewer re-asks and no format failures, not accuracy.
Suggested follow-up, not done here: combine with a tighter floor (e.g. b1r0g2's 0.9). Greedy decoding then makes the veto's correction deterministic too.
